[
(780, induction on N, and lower bound on Z/N),
(28/2, CLT of H and proof by contradiction of Z>N)
]
Then you check that your new proposal is not in that list. If it is, you try again.

Ex "I am thinking there could be a hint in the upper bound. I will check it out. Ahh, I see I made a mistake. But now the size formula seems really promising!" 
"Then formalize and submit answer when you think you have something. While you know the rejector is skeptical, you really try to find the right answer every try.

A plane $\mathcal{P}$ intersects a rectangular prism at a hexagon which has side lengths $45,66,63,55,54$, and 77, in that order. Compute the distance from the center of the rectangular prism to $\mathcal{P}$..<<

You proposal cannot be in this this list. Try again and submit a new unique answer."

PlanECLIPSE
- Core idea: Use a tight geometric reduction with an invariant-based elimination to reduce to a single polynomial in the distance δ from the prism center to the plane, then verify with a feasible prism (half-sides a, b, c) and plane normal n.
- Model setup
  - Prism with half-sides a, b, c > 0; center at origin.
  - Plane P: n · x = δ, where n = (u, v, w) with |n| = 1, δ is the signed distance from origin to P.
  - The six hexagon edges arise from intersections of P with the six faces x = ±a, y = ±b, z = ±c, taken in the hexagon order corresponding to the given edge sequence.
- Unknowns and constraints
  - Unknowns: a, b, c, u, v, w, δ plus six edge-length parameters L1..L6 with L1..L6 = 45, 66, 63, 55, 54, 77.
  - Equations: For each face, compute the line of intersection with P; the distance between successive intersection points on P gives Li. Include the unit-norm constraint u^2 + v^2 + w^2 = 1.
- Elimination plan
  - Symbolically eliminate a, b, c, u, v, w in a staged fashion (possibly leveraging symmetry of the hexagon) to obtain a polynomial equation solely in δ with rational coefficients.
  - Look for real roots δ that yield a,b,c > 0 and a valid unit normal n.
- Verification plan
  - For each candidate δ, solve for a, b, c and n (or at least confirm existence) that reproduce the six edge lengths in the given order.
  - Ensure the reconstructed geometry is feasible (positive half-sides, real numbers).
- Deliverable
  - A concrete δ-polynomial with rational coefficients, real roots for δ, and a corresponding feasible set (a, b, c, n) verifying the hexagon.
